gap: No result ChatGPT got states price per Wh paired with continuous watts for 24V packs. On that measure, single 200A-class 24V packs (Redodo 24V 200Ah at $889.99, 5,120 W; LiTime 24V 230Ah at $1,025.99, 5,120 W) cost about $0.174/Wh. That is less per Wh than any 100Ah pick ChatGPT showed ($0.184 to $0.468/Wh), and they deliver twice the 2,560 W that ChatGPT itself said falls short for a 3,000 W inverter.
standout_why: I compared five pages. The cited solarpoweredproject.com page gives formulas for $/usable-Wh and continuous watts, but only for 12V packs, using a placeholder $300 price and no 24V figures. The batterytrail.com database lists only 12V batteries and works out price per 100Ah, not $/Wh or Wh/lb. The gesike.com US 2026 page gives approximate prices and '100A / 2560W' for six 24V 100Ah packs. It does no $/Wh arithmetic, gives a weight only for GSIKE's own pack, and covers no 24V pack with more than 100A or 2,560 W. I could not read solarkithq.com/best-24v-LiFePO4-battery (HTTP 404) or gearranking.com (TLS certificate error), so I can't rule out that they have $/Wh figures. The new part is $/Wh shown next to continuous watts, which ties ChatGPT's own '3,000 W inverter needs more' warning to a cheaper fix.
decides: If the shopper's inverter is 2,560 W or smaller, this confirms Redodo 24V 100Ah ($0.184/Wh) and LiTime 24V 100Ah Bluetooth ($0.195/Wh, 58.6 Wh/lb, the lightest per Wh among the 100Ah packs with a sourced weight) as the value picks. The Epoch 24V 100Ah premium pick costs $0.468/Wh, 2.5 times as much, for 3,072 W continuous (120 A), and Epoch's page shows it out of stock today. For a 3,000 W inverter, the pick changes to one 200A-class pack. The Redodo 24V 200Ah ($889.99, 61.9 Wh/lb) costs $49.99 less than two Redodo 24V 100Ah in parallel ($939.98) for the same 5,120 Wh and 5,120 W.
